newsitem.title: TAIWAN: One dead as police quell Taiwan youth prison riot.
newsitem.headline: One dead as police quell Taiwan youth prison riot.

text.p: Police handcuffed and shackled some 320 inmates at a juvenile detention centre late on Thursday, clamping down on Taiwan's worst prison violence in 14 years that claimed at least one life.

State-run television showed the youths, many lying on the ground as they waited for transfer to another centre, being kicked by a warden while parents frantically pounded the prison gate demanding to see their sons.
"They are not animals, they are humans!" one mother shouted.

The northern Hsinchu centre has barred all visitors to the compound since violence erupted on Tuesday. In a riot that lasted over 24 hours, inmates torched their cells, smashed a workshop and briefly held a supervisor hostage, prompting police to fire blanks and tear gas.
Police transferred 90 alleged participants to a centre in central Taichung city early on Wednesday while hundreds of other inmates shouted and banged on their cell bars.
Authorities locked up and removed 320 more juveniles late on Wednesday. But one of the youths died apparently of a heart attack while on the transfer.
"The inmate was rushed to a hospital, which initially diagnosed him as dying of heart failure," the state-run Taiwan Television quoted unnamed hospital sources as saying.
Hsinchu warden Lee Ching-yuan said the juvenile, 16-year-old Lu Mo-hsien, might have been beaten by fellow inmates during the chaos.
"My initial understanding is that he probably got beaten by other inmates," Lee said. "I issue my apology to the society for what happened."
The melee began on Tuesday afternoon when the offenders, protesting harsh working conditions and stringent parole requirements, used sticks and steel bars to smash up an electronics workshop.
They seized a supervisor but soon released him. He was slightly injured along with an inmate trying to protect him from rioters.
More than 700 civilian and military police were deployed for the standoff. Three firetrucks were used to extinguish small cell fires ignited by inmates.
Prison officials said they were investigating. The prison violence was Taiwan's worst since 1982, when the same Hsinchu compound was the scene of two riots.
